summary: Discovery + POC scope focused on selecting open-model candidates for a 6-week pilot to power clinical triage and patient messaging. Key success criteria: p95 latency < 350ms (in-region), hallucination rate < 3% on clinical QA sets, throughput 120 QPS steady with 2x burst, and support for English + Spanish. Timeline: 2-week quick eval -> 4-week pilot with hosted benchmarks -> decision point.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-30
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Liam Brenner (Redwood AE), Maya Patel (SE), Carlos Ortega (SE), Nina Zhao (CSM) — Marta, Dan, Priya, Omar, Eve (WillowCare)

[00:00] Liam Brenner: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you making time. quick intro — i'm liam, AE for the region, with maya and carlos on the eng side. nina's here for success and handover.
[00:08] Marta Ruiz: Hi all — thanks. we wanted to get alignment on model choices and what success looks like for a pilot. we run patient triage flows and internal knowledge search, mostly English and Spanish. latency's a big deal for chat flows.
[00:18] Maya Patel: great, quick agenda: clarify success criteria, dig into workload numbers, propose open-model shortlist and tradeoffs, agree benchmarks & timeline. sound good?
[00:28] Dan Cho: yup. also curious about cost/latency tradeoffs and private deployment options — we have PHI concerns.
[00:35] Liam Brenner: we'll cover hosting modes — hosted first, then dedicated/private if needed.
[00:39] 
[00:45] Carlos Ortega: can we start with success criteria specifics? what would you accept in this pilot?
[00:49] Priya Singh: for product: p95 latency under 350ms for chat, typical message size 80 tokens outgoing, 40 tokens incoming. hallucination tolerance is low — we'd want <3% on a clinical QA set and deterministic citing for med facts. throughput target is 120 QPS steady-state with 2x burst for peak hours.
[01:10] Maya Patel: good, that's concrete. when you say clinical QA set — how large, and do you have labels?
[01:15] Marta Ruiz: we can provide ~500 labeled Q&A items and a broader 3k unlabelled prompts. we'll annotate the 500 for precision/recall checks.
[01:23] Omar El-Khatib: also multilingual — English and Spanish roughly 70/30 traffic split. we care about translation quality and domain-specific terminology.
[01:30] Nina Zhao: noted. on compliance Eve, anything additional?
[01:33] Eve Thomas: SOC2 is mandatory, encryption at rest with customer KMS ideally, and audit logs per request for 90 days. we might need an on-prem option later, but initial pilot can be hosted if data is redacted and we can sign a DPA.
[01:49] 
[02:00] Liam Brenner: good constraints. model shortlist — we propose three open-model classes:
[02:06] - LlamaX-13B (quantized float16/8 variants): strong cost/latency, OK on medical QA after light prompting
[02:13] - Galactica-derived open-med models (specialized): better factuality on clinical facts but larger and maybe slower
[02:20] - Mistral/Owl-family 7B-16B hybrids (dense + optimizer kernels): good multilingual support and low latency when quantized
[02:28] 
[02:30] Marta Ruiz: are those the actual names? our legal prefers not to use brand names for public docs, but yes the categories are fine. which ones tend to hallucinate less?
[02:37] Carlos Ortega: domain-tuned models (the galactica-derived) often have better recall on medical facts but can still hallucinate; we mitigate with retrieval augmentation and a reranker. the smaller dense models with strong token kernels can be faster but may lose niche terminology.
[02:48] Dan Cho: retrieval augmentation — do you mean hooking up to our clinical KB?
[02:52] Maya Patel: yep, prefix retrieval: preface model with top-k docs, and use a reranker to verify. we'll include that in the benchmark harness.
[02:59] 
[03:05] Priya Singh: talk to me about latency numbers — if we do hosted, can you hit p95 <350ms for 80 token responses?
[03:10] Carlos Ortega: for quantized 7-13B families running in-region on our hosted infra, yes typical p95 is 150–300ms depending on batching. for 16–30B models usually above 400ms unless we allow more aggressive quantization or dedicated GPUs.
[03:27] Omar El-Khatib: and cost differential?
[03:30] Liam Brenner: rough thumb — 7B quantized may be 0.3x the cost of a 13B float path; 13B quant quant about 0.6x of 13B fp16. 30B models can be 2-4x cost. we'll provide a detailed per-token cost table.
[03:43] 
[03:50] Marta Ruiz: we prioritize accuracy over cost but need cost to be predictably low enough for production. what's your recommended POC approach?
[03:56] Maya Patel: two-stage: 1) 2-week quick eval: run 3 candidate models with retrieval and reranker on a subset (500 labeled test). measure hallucination, p95 latency, and per-token cost. 2) 4-week pilot: choose best candidate and run full traffic simulation (3k prompts, steady 120 QPS) with logging and safety hooks. decision at week 6.
[04:20] Priya Singh: timelines fine. who owns the test harness?
[04:24] Liam Brenner: Redwood will own benchmark harness and provide a repro script; we need WillowCare to supply prompts and sample traffic trace.
[04:31] 
[04:36] Dan Cho: about private deployment — what's gating and effort?
[04:39] Maya Patel: private means we deploy our control plane in your VPC or on-prem bundle. initial pilot hosted, if compliance or KMS requirements block us, we can stage a private deployment; expect 4–8 weeks onboarding depending on networking.
[04:54] Eve Thomas: noted, might need HSM support for keys later.
[04:58] 
[05:05] Carlos Ortega: benchmark metrics we propose capturing: p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, cost per 1k tokens, factuality/hallucination rate on labeled set, answer recall/precision for triage labels, and Spanish/EN split accuracy. also cold-start and burst behavior.
[05:21] Omar El-Khatib: for Spanish, do you expect the models to degrade significantly?
[05:25] Maya Patel: some models are trained more on English and will drop. our shortlist includes at least one model family known for multilingual pretraining. we'll quantify via translation and native Spanish prompts.
[05:36] 
[05:40] Marta Ruiz: any recommended quantization settings? we worry about quality drop.
[05:44] Carlos Ortega: start with 8-bit quant for evaluation; if quality holds then test 4-bit quant with per-channel scale for the best candidate. we track ROC curves on the labeled set to compare.
[05:55] 
[06:00] Priya Singh: what about safety — we need guardrails for clinical advice.
[06:04] Maya Patel: safety layers: instruction-level filtering, retrieval-based citation requirement, and post-generation classifier to catch unsafe outputs. we'll include a safety metric in the benchmark that flags any clinical advice not supported by retrieval docs.
[06:18] 
[06:25] Liam Brenner: vendor lock questions — we're using open models so you retain portability. we can also provide an export package if you want to run on-prem later.
[06:35] Dan Cho: nice.
[06:38] 
[06:45] Marta Ruiz: on the shortlist matrix — can you show sample quality tradeoffs in writing?
[06:49] Liam Brenner: yes — we'll share a matrix with expected p95, baseline hallucination % (from similar verticals), cost/kg (per token), and multilingual rank.
[06:58] 
[07:05] Carlos Ortega: quick note on benchmarking: want to confirm tokenization rules — are you using UTF-8 whitespace tokenization or do you have special medical tokenization?
[07:14] Omar El-Khatib: we use some custom tokens for med shorthand, could provide a token map.
[07:18] Maya Patel: please share that; mismatched tokenization skews latency and token-cost numbers.
[07:25] 
[07:30] Priya Singh: performance SLOs — if one model meets accuracy but slightly misses latency, what's the remediation?
[07:36] Maya Patel: options: quantize further, increase instance count (scale), or pick a lower-latency model and add routing to the better-quality one only for complex queries. Redwood supports smart routing and fallback to dedicated pools.
[07:49] 
[07:55] Marta Ruiz: stakeholders for decision: me (ML), Priya (product), Eve (compliance). timeline for decision is end of pilot at week 6.
[08:05] Liam Brenner: perfect. any other constraints?
[08:09] Eve Thomas: retention policy — we need logs but PII redaction by default. can you redact before storing?
[08:15] Maya Patel: we can do inline redaction and store redacted logs, and provide unredacted logs to you under stricter controls if needed.
[08:23] 
[08:30] Dan Cho: are there existing benchmarks from Redwood on similar healthcare clients we can see?
[08:34] Liam Brenner: yes we'll share anonymized benchmarks and a sample benchmark spreadsheet.
[08:38] 
[08:45] Carlos Ortega: technical deep-dive offer: if you want, we can provision a micro-benchmark this week with one of the 7B models on your sample prompt set — give us 48 hours to spin up and run quick checks.
[08:56] Omar El-Khatib: that would be great.
[09:00] 
[09:05] Priya Singh: ok recap and next steps?
[09:07] Liam Brenner: recap: 1) Redwood shares shortlist + matrix + benchmark plan by 04-02. 2) WillowCare shares labeled 500 test and 3k prompts + token map by 04-06. 3) Redwood runs quick micro-bench (48–72h) and then scheduled full hosted benchmark wk of 04-13. 4) compliance doc access for SOC2/KMS by 04-05. decision at end of 6-week pilot.
[09:30] Marta Ruiz: agreed. thanks everyone.
[09:33] Liam Brenner: thanks all, we'll follow up with calendar invites and the docs.

[09:45] Meeting ends
